Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightMode_tooltip: How night is decided. Fixed hours: night runs between the two hours below, every day of the year, whatever the Day/Night Cycle setting. Seasonal night: the game's own dusk and dawn, which move with the seasons and follow the Day/Night Cycle setting (endless day has no night, endless night is always night).
Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightStartHour_toolt: Hour of the day, 0 to 23, at which night begins when Night mode is Fixed hours. Night can run past midnight. If both hours are the same there is no night at all, and the log says so.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightEndHour_tooltip: Hour of the day, 0 to 23, at which night ends when Night mode is Fixed hours.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Day_tooltip: What changes by day while no event runs. Fields are key=value, separated by ;. speed=+25 makes 25 percent of ordinary zombies one tier faster (shambler to fast shambler, fast shambler to sprinter) and speed=-50 makes 50 percent one tier slower; a zombie that speeds up is among the last to slow down, and speed=0 keeps every zombie at the game's speed. steps=2 moves them two tiers: always sprinters or always shamblers. health=0.7 gives new and reloaded zombies 70 percent of the health they roll and lowers any zombie above 70 percent of the most a new one can have; health=1.5 gives new and reloaded zombies 150 percent, and zombies already around keep theirs. Both can grow with the days since the world began: speed=+25..+75;grow=60d goes from +25 on world day 0 to +75 on world day 60 and stays there, grow=30d..90d moves it between those days instead, and health=0.7..0.4 works the same way. World days are counted at noon, as for every= and mindays=, and a speed share is rounded to a whole percent. A range needs grow= in the same definition, and grow= moves only that definition's own ranges. Monsters of every kind, Bandits and crawlers keep their own speed and are never capped; the health factor is given as the game creates a zombie, before it marks some of them, so a reloaded crawler or a new mutant may get it too. off=cof,mutants turns those monster kinds off (off=none turns none off): far ones are removed, The Mutants makes no new mutants and Cry of Fear Monster NPCs spawns nothing new. A kind no definition turns off is left alone. For Cry of Fear monsters only at night, write off=cof here and keep its own Night only option off; as with that option, each time cof is on again every Cry of Fear home may be filled again, so killed monsters come back too. set.Table.Option=value changes a sandbox option, for example set.ZombieLore.Toughness=1, or set.Option=value for an option without a table, for example set.HoursForCorpseRemoval=24; it goes back to its base value when the day ends. say=text shows a line to every player when the day begins (say=@Key shows that translation), and color=rrggbb gives its colour. sound=Name plays that game sound on every player's game at the same moment, with or without a line, for example sound=MetaWolfHowl; upper and lower case matter. A sun event starts from these values. The default, speed=+25;health=0.7, makes a quarter of the zombies faster and the zombies more fragile. A bad field is skipped and logged, and the rest applies.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Night_tooltip: What changes by night while no event runs, written as for Day: speed=-50 or speed=+25, steps=2, health=1.5, a range that grows such as speed=-25..-75;grow=60d, off=mutants,cof or off=none, set.Table.Option=value, say=text, color=rrggbb and sound=Name. The values go back to their base when the night ends. A moon event starts from these values, even when it runs into the day. The default, speed=-50;off=mutants, makes half of the zombies slower, keeps The Mutants from making mutants at night and removes far mutants.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Events1_tooltip: Moons and suns: special nights and days. Events are separated by |, fields by ;. Each event needs id=name (letters a-z, digits and _) and track=moon (decided when night begins) or track=sun (decided when day begins). Conditions, which must all hold: moon=full (the first night of a full moon; also new, waxingcrescent, firstquarter, waxinggibbous, waninggibbous, thirdquarter, waningcrescent), date=10-31 or date=12-20..01-05, month=6..8, season=summer, every=30 (every 30 days since the world began; every=30+5 shifts it by 5), mindays=30 and maxdays=365 (days since the world began), nth=4 (every 4th time its calendar conditions hold), after=id (the first time after that event ended), cooldown=20d or 36h, interval=3d..7d (after each start it waits a random 3 to 7 whole days, counted in world days, before it can happen again, and the first wait counts from the world's start; interval=7d waits exactly 7 days, interval=12h..36h whole hours from its start time; once the wait is over it stays a candidate until it starts, so a lost chance or a higher prio doesn't roll a new wait, and an admin start counts as a start), weather=rain, snow, storm, fog or clear, tempmin=0 and tempmax=30 (degrees C), chance=50. A list such as moon=full,new holds when any item does. Timing: at=HH:MM starts it later in its night or day, and for=phase (the default), 2p (phases), 6h or 3.5d sets how long it lasts. prio=10: when several events qualify, the highest is tried first. Effects: speed, steps, health, off, set., say, color and sound, as in Day and Night, with grow= for its own ranges; a moon starts from Night and a sun from Day, and a range it takes from them grows with their grow=. One event runs at a time, and nothing else is decided while it runs. An event with an error is skipped and logged. Keep each option under 32000 bytes.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Events2_tooltip: More events, written as in Events 1. The option an event is in only matters between events with the same prio: earlier ones are tried first.

Sandbox_Crepuscular_Kinds_tooltip: Monsters of other mods, told by their outfit: name=prefix,prefix;name=prefix, for example wraiths=ZW_,Wraith;husks=Husk_. A zombie whose outfit name starts with one of the prefixes (upper and lower case don't matter) belongs to that kind. Names are made of a-z, 0-9 and _. cof (Cry of Fear Monster NPCs) and mutants (The Mutants) are built in, and other mods can add kinds of their own. Put a kind in off= of Day, Night or an event to remove its far members while that applies; it can't keep a mod from turning zombies into its monsters. When The Mutants is loaded, members of every kind are never turned into mutants.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_KeepDistance_tooltip: While a kind is off, a member of it is removed only if it has no target and no player is within this many tiles of it, in a straight line. 0 to 300. Keep it beyond what players can see, or monsters vanish in view.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RemovalsPerMinute_to: Most far monsters of kinds that are off removed per in-game minute, all kinds together, 1 to 500. Every player's game is told to remove its copy of each one.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_MutantRequeue_toolti: Only matters when The Mutants is loaded. On: when mutants come back on (the definition in effect no longer has off=mutants), the zombies already loaded are offered to The Mutants, up to 200 per in-game minute, so the ones it picks turn into mutants at once. Some may change in plain view. Off: The Mutants only looks at a zombie when it is next created or loaded.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_ZombiesPerSweep_tool: Zombies checked each in-game minute, 50 to 5000, on the server and on every player's game, for the speed and health of the definition in effect. After a change it takes about the number of loaded zombies divided by this many minutes until every zombie has it; more costs more time each minute.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Notifications_toolti: On: when a definition begins, every player sees its line (say=) and hears its sound (sound=). Off: no player sees or hears any of them, and the events still run as before. Admins still get the replies of the Crepuscular menu and the line about definitions with errors.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Verbose_tooltip: Writes phase changes, each decision with its rolls, event starts and ends, sandbox value changes, removals of far monsters and mutant requeues to the log, prefixed [Crepuscular]. Warnings and errors, such as mistakes in the definitions, are always logged.
